title: The misleading indicator: averages, vanity metrics and hidden denominators

videos.script: Monday morning, and Renata's report says the average order on the new garden pages is two thousand six hundred reais. {{report}} The shop's usual order is three hundred and fifty. The room is pleased. Nobody made a mistake. Two orders from one hotel did that. {{correct}} This lesson is about numbers that are correct and still mislead. They are more dangerous than wrong ones, because nothing about them looks broken. {{five}} There are five shapes, and you will compute each one in your spreadsheet. An average that describes nobody. A total that can only grow. {{denominator}} A complaint rate that falls and rises at once, depending on what you divide by. {{stores}} Two stores, where the one that is better at every kind of delivery comes out worse overall. {{small}} And a rise of two hundred percent that turns out to be two complaints. {{cure}} For each, the cure is the same. Put back the thing the number left out.
